answer_text: Line one copies the problem; line two removes brackets, ending in minus four; line three groups like terms with two minus four; line four is three x squared plus four x minus two. Your combining is right, but the result is wrong because of a sign slip when removing the second brackets. Check what happens when you subtract negative four.

Your page shows the original equation, then x squared minus six x plus seven equals zero, followed by completing the square, taking square roots, and isolating x. Your last step follows correctly from the previous line, but there’s an earlier division slip in line two. When you divide the equation by two, what needs to happen to the constant seven?

Your page shows one point two five plus zero point eight seven five, rewritten with an extra zero, then addition by place, ending with two point zero two five litres. Your work has one slip: you carried one from the hundredths but left it out when adding the tenths. Check the tenths again, including that carried one.

Your page shows the original function, u equals x plus one, v equals x minus two, both derivatives equal one, then a derivative simplifying from x plus one minus x plus two over x minus two squared to three over x minus two squared. The result is wrong: the quotient-rule numerator’s subtraction order is reversed. Check which product should come first in that numerator.

You wrote: at least two women equals all minus zero women minus one woman; thirteen choose five equals 1287; seven choose five equals 21; six choose one equals six; and 1287 minus 21 minus six equals 1260. Your latest result is wrong because the one-woman case undercounts committees. After choosing one woman, how many ways can you choose the four men needed?

The page shows A and B, expands both products, gives A B rows zero, three and minus six, fifteen, gives B A rows two, eleven and minus four, seventeen, and says they differ. Your conclusion is right, but A B has a sign slip in its top-left entry; the other entries are right. Recheck the product of minus one and minus two.
